newsitem.title: CANADA: INSTANT VIEW - Canada January CPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Canada January CPI.

text.p: Following are reactions to January consumer price data released by Statistics Canada on Friday.

Economists in a Reuters survey had forecast, on average, the unadjusted CPI to rise 0.25 percent on the month. The survey also forecast a 2.2 percent year-over-year rise in the all-items and 0.15 percent month-on-month rise in the core CPI.
Michael Gregory, economist, Lehman Brothers - "Boring...But on the other hand, this is exactly where the central bank would like to see inflation at this stage."
Doug Porter, economist, Nesbitt Burns Inc - "There was no major surprise in the number. In fact, it was almost bang on expectations -- that's the overall number.

"But on the core, I would say there is still some very good news in that seasonally adjusted prices excluding food and energy were flat on the month -- and that's certainly one of the best performances we have seen in the past year.
"So I would say the underlying message is that inflation is still no problem in this country and we will probably actually see the year-over-year rate move a little bit lower in the months ahead."

Randall Powley, senior economist, ScotiaMcLeod Inc -- "I was a little disappointed because I was hoping for a bit more discounting...There was no clear evidence of it so that was a little bit bearish.
"But all of the big increases were not related to markets.
"So I am neutral to slightly bearish on the report, but all-in-all, there were no big surprises."
